artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission ruled on a matter involving Metropolitan New York Presbytery's handling of a session that permitted a woman to expound Scripture during worship and held services without sermons. The SJC remitted the matter to the Presbytery to complete its work and report to the Committee on Review of Presbytery Records, while critiquing the procedural manner in which the matter was referred to the SJC.

artifacts.synopsis: Tennessee Valley Presbytery approved without exception Session minutes planning a youth group Super Bowl Party on Sunday; the SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in its constitutional interpretation. A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Neal Ganzel appealed his conviction and six-month suspension by Central Florida Presbytery for abuse of spiritual authority and related charges. The SJC unanimously sustained both specifications of error, finding that CFP violated BCO 32-20's one-year statute of limitations for most charges and committed numerous procedural missteps that rendered the disciplinary process significantly flawed and prejudicial, reversing the entire censure.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Daniel Schrock and others complained that Philadelphia Presbytery failed to properly judge and record the nature of TE Larry Smith's views on the continuation of spiritual gifts of prophecy and tongues when it admitted him by transfer, as required by BCO 21-4e,f and RAO 16-3.e.5. The SJC sustained the complaint by a vote of 14-5-2 and remanded the matter to Presbytery to receive a written statement from TE Smith and make a proper determination, with a substantial dissent arguing the Presbytery had in fact complied with the Constitution and that RAO 16-3.e.5 is not part of the BCO.

artifacts.synopsis: Bumgarner, a ruling elder who had been deposed in 2012, filed a BCO 40-5 application in 2015 seeking reversal of the censure after having previously withdrawn his complaint and acknowledged it could not be resubmitted. The SJC dismissed the application as administratively out of order because it sought to re-file a withdrawn complaint and because BCO 40-3 prohibits reversal of judicial censures except by appeal or complaint.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC reported that South Florida Presbytery responded to the citation issued by the 43rd General Assembly. The SJC found most responses satisfactory, but found one response unsatisfactory (regarding charges against a TE that were not properly processed under BCO 32-2), and noted an additional exception of substance regarding improper divestiture under BCO 46-8.

artifacts.title: Presbytery authority to remove censure of suspended or deposed teaching elder

matches.evidence: A new presbytery may remove censures of suspension or deposition only with the original presbytery's permission or after satisfying BCO 37-7 procedures; the original presbytery retains recourse under BCO 40-3 through 40-5.

artifacts.title: Review and control action while a judicial case is pending on appeal

matches.evidence: A higher court may note an exception through review and control but may take no action on it while judicial proceedings are pending; the effect of any unconstitutional act is suspended upon appeal.

artifacts.title: Mandatory review of all previously unreviewed session minutes

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that it is mandatory for a presbytery to review all previously unreviewed session records, not merely resume with current ones.

artifacts.title: CRPR review scope for presbyteries with pending judicial cases

matches.evidence: The CCB found a proposed CRPR amendment addressing judicial cases and CRPR review under RAO 16-3.e.8 to be not in constitutional conflict.
